reason: The text describes Jacob as a leader commanding obedience from his people and servants. Jacob sends messengers with his instructions (וַיְצַו אֹתָם לֵאמֹר - 'he commanded them saying'), divides his household according to his judgment (וַיַּחַץ אֶת־ הָעָם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּוֹ - 'he divided the people with him'), and his wives and children bow before him as he bows before Esau. No antagonism, resistance, or conflict between Jacob and his followers is mentioned or implied. Jacob's fear is directed toward his brother Esau, not toward his own people. The people appear obedient and compliant throughout the narrative.
